classification_reason: All ten arrivals were handled: nine filed through receipted gateway writes after one batch approval, one deliberately not filed, and each got a connection list. But the product cannot create a new note from a capture, note.revise has no preview, and almost every cross-course connection came from my reading rather than a product query.

consumer.goal: File ten captures (A01, A02, A05, A07, A10, A13, A14, A21, A22, A24) and tell the learner, for each, what older material it connects to.
consumer.first_action: Read the drop metadata and all ten arrivals, then read ARCHITECTURE §5.3/§5.6, WORKFLOWS §17/§23 and the shelving/review/note-revise capability definitions to find a governed destination for each kind.
commands: ls system/schema; grep shelving in docs
validate --compact; warning_baseline --check; los generate; los operations
confusions: Durable-understanding captures without an active stage (BN reading page, a friend's guest-lecture notes, a textbook excerpt) have no note-creation capability. WORKFLOWS §17 describes minting a new transcribed note, but no gateway write does that. The shelving path (review.prepare/apply) is admitted only as a UI gesture, and its items-file format is not documented. I appended to the most relevant existing note with note.revise instead (§8: prefer updating an existing note).
note.revise has no preflight or diff: the bare command only says 'requires --approve after reviewing the full replacement', so the reviewable diff had to be produced outside the product.
Which expected_revisions key note.revise wants is undocumented; {note_id: 0} happened to be right.
Arrival dates for A21, A22 and A24 (2026-09-26/27) are after today's date (2026-09-25); I kept them in the provenance headers as given.

After the writes, `los operations` showed one operation with 21 attempts, all AMBIGUOUS. Root cause: this container exports TRACEPARENT, and every los call adopts its trace and span id (confirmed on a scratch copy); F-s03-diag-ambiguous-01 was updated.
corrective_steps: My first batch run failed before reaching the gateway because my own script used a relative envelope path ('no such structured input'); fixed and re-ran. This was my own harness error, not a product failure.
From here on I ran los with TRACEPARENT unset so diagnostics stay per-request (recorded as a deviation).
questions_asked_to_learner: Presented the ten-row plan (destination, capability and exact appended text for each; A24 not filed) and asked for approval → scripted reply: 'Approved — apply what you showed me, nothing else.'
Is the sourdough schedule worth keeping? → treated per scripted reply: 'Your call. If it's not study material, don't make it a note.'
consumer.outcome: Nine captures filed with receipts: six into the working notes of the stages they belong to, three appended verbatim (with a provenance header) to an existing note of the learner's. The sourdough schedule was not filed. Each arrival got a ranked list of older material it connects to (connections.jsonl, after-shelving). Validation 0 errors, no new warning signature, views regenerated. Changes remain uncommitted in the world.

internal.transaction_behavior: Nine independent transactions, each with a snapshot guard (fresh snapshot fetched via bootstrap --brief before each), one artifact revision bumped 0→1 (unit for stage notes, note id for note.revise), before/after file hashes in the receipt. note.revise wrote exactly the approved bytes (sha256 matches the replacement file) and left the frontmatter unchanged.
internal.approval_behavior: operator-approval over channel operator, subject = intent hash; the learner's batch approval preceded the envelopes. note.revise additionally binds the replacement file by SHA-256.
internal.projection_activity: Snapshot advanced with every write; `los generate` republished the manifest once at the end.
internal.persistence_activity: 9 receipts added; idempotency.yaml and revisions.yaml updated; traces appended (all under the inherited trace id).
internal.derived_changes: 3 derived files modified (manifest and views), +10 KB.
warnings_errors: los operations: all requests merged into one AMBIGUOUS operation (TRACEPARENT inheritance)
internal.git_diff_stat: 10 files changed, 130 insertions(+), 0 deletions (cumulative with S04's 13 lines); 10 new untracked receipts

friction.description: No governed way to create a new durable note from a capture (WORKFLOWS §3/§17 describe it; only analysis-notes, atlas questions and UI-only shelving can create notes). Three captures had to be appended to existing notes instead.
friction.cost: ~5 tool calls of capability/doc reading; a filing compromise

friction.description: note.revise offers no --check/diff; a full replacement file must be assembled by hand and the diff shown to the learner outside the product.
`los operations` presents successful writes as AMBIGUOUS/needs_attention when TRACEPARENT is present in the environment.

per_arrival.why: Sourdough feeding schedule — not study material; per the learner's rule, not made into a note (and not put into the inbox).

scenario_record.connection_records: connections.jsonl probes A01, A02, A05, A07, A10, A13, A14, A21, A22, A24 (phase after-shelving)

uncertainties: Appending a friend's notes (A10) or a textbook excerpt (A13) to a user-authored note changes that note's authorship mix; I marked each section's provenance but did not change the frontmatter (authorship still 'user').
Whether A05 and A14 complete their stages is the learner's call; I did not update progress.
